subject: dwarfBlacksmith
pitch:
Category: Humanoid character.
Subject: dwarf blacksmith at an anvil.
Style: Blizzard/Warcraft.
reasoning:
I'm planning a compact but detailed module for a stocky dwarf blacksmith figure, Warcraft-style, with a braided beard, leather apron, raised hammer, and an anvil with glowing iron, keeping proportions chunky and around 1.4 meters tall.

I'm working out the skeleton: hips at the base, a spine chain running up through chest to neck and head, legs positioned in a wide stance with feet near the anvil, and arms rigged so the right holds a raised hammer while the left rests near the anvil gripping a glowing bar, defining joint coordinates and chain names for each segment.

I'm adding a jaw joint beneath the head for the beard attachment, then moving on to building the torso using a loft shape driven by the spine bone with stations defining width and height at each point.

Repositioning the apron as an extruded polygon shape rigged to the spine, narrow at top and wider at bottom, with leather texturing and a scorched bottom edge. Now I'm setting up the leg bones, mirroring hip positions for both sides.

Setting ankle target with the boot box positioned to cover the sole and toe, using a three-name chain so the limb function produces a tip joint for the foot. I'll sweep the leg chain with tapering radii for the boot shape.

For the arms, I'm setting shoulder positions and giving each side a different pose: left arm reaches down to hold tongs near the anvil top, while the right arm raises up with a hammer, working out target coordinates for hand placement on each side.

Setting up the arm chains with shoulder, elbow, and hand joints parented to the spine, sized with appropriate sweep radii. For the dwarf's look I'm going with bare muscular arms and a sleeveless shirt, adding leather/metal shoulder pauldrons with rivets for that Warcraft aesthetic.

Now I'm building fist-shaped hands with simple sphere geometry, and working out the hammer—a handle rod extending from the raised hand upward with the head positioned above it for that classic raised-weapon pose.

Confirming the head's long axis stays horizontal along z so the striking faces point front/back as it swings, keeping the handle tilted slightly and attached to the hand joint via a rod primitive. Now I'm positioning the left hand holding tongs with a glowing bar resting on the anvil.

I'm orienting the anvil with its long axis along x and horn pointing +x, then placing the glowing bar along x on the anvil's top surface, with tongs rendered as two rods connecting the left hand to the bar's near end so the hammer can strike it.

Still shaping anvil geometry...

Still plotting coordinates...

Placing the glowing orange hot bar on top, positioning the hands and tongs around it, and adding tiny spark elements for effect. Now setting up a cylindrical stump near the base.

For the dwarf's head, I'm working out proportions: a sphere centered above the neck, with a bushy iron-gray braided beard, steel goggles pushed up on the forehead, thick brows, mustache, and a prominent nose, planning to use textured planes for facial details.

Building the mustache as a swept curve drooping from under the nose to the sides, tapering from thick to thin, and planning a large beard as a lofted shape running down the chin to the chest with possible braided sections.

I'm adding braided beads along the braid sweeps with gold ring ties at the ends, plus scattered hair-strand card textures across the beard surface for a fur-like look. For the hairstyle, I'm leaning toward a bald dwarf look with a defined brow ridge, maybe paired with a leather accessory.

Deciding instead to give him a small orange mohawk, extruding a zigzag crest shape along the top of the head to form spiked blades positioned near the skull's peak.

Now adding small flattened spheres for ears, then placing goggles on the forehead—brass torus rings with glowing blue lenses, plus a strap swept as a closed curve looping around the head at an appropriate radius and tilt to match the skull's curvature.

Calculating goggle lens placement against the curved head surface, with glass glowing amber like forge light, and positioning the mohawk ridge to sit just behind the goggles around the brow line.

Now I'm working out the shoulder pauldrons as hemisphere domes tilted outward with a rotation offset so they naturally cap the shoulder and angle upward-outward, attaching them to the spine2 bone.

Then I'm figuring out the belt geometry by interpolating the waist's elliptical cross-section between hip and torso stations to get an appropriate radius at belt height, plus adding small spike cones on top of the pauldrons and painting them steel with gold trim.

I need to add a pelvis loft station below the waist so the loft has at least two points before reaching hips, then route the belt sweep as a closed curve with a gold buckle box at the front.

For the lower body, I'm planning cloth-colored pants sweeps from hip to knee covered by boots, then adding boot geometry: a leather box shape, an ankle cuff cylinder, and a small steel toe cap box at the front.

I'm adding a fur trim ring at the boot top and noting the stump rests directly on the ground with no floor needed. For the shirt and skin, I'm using mottled cloth coloring and mottled skin tones, plus small belt items like a pouch and hammer, and planning a glow effect for a heated bar using a gradient.

Still writing bar glow sections and spark effects...

Adding the hammer with a steel head, banded leather-wrapped handle, and decal runes on the head.

Normalizing the handle direction, I compute the top of the hammer head at roughly (-0.3, 1.88, 0.42) — raised above the dwarf's head without overlap. Checking proportions against the hand, head, and shoulder positions, the arm bends naturally from shoulder to raised hand, so the pose reads correctly.

For the fist, I'll use a small skin-colored box with simplified finger geometry rather than individual sphere fingers, keeping it cheap but readable. I'll attach parts to the arm bone chain using joint names, apply paint-based coloring to each part, and add decal textures for the eye, runes, hair strands, and an anvil-and-hammer crest on the apron front.

Now I'm figuring out the apron's placement and dimensions relative to the torso loft, checking front-facing z-offsets at different heights (chest, belly, pelvis) so the apron sits just in front of the body without clipping, and adding a small belt buckle emblem to match the crest motif.

Working out shoulder placement relative to torso width and arm radius, then sizing a shoulder ball to cover the joint gap. Also planning scattered fur tufts across the beard surface for texture.

Now I'm thinking through the jaw structure — separating it from the head sphere, positioning a small jaw joint beneath the mouth, and letting the beard hide most of it.

Setting up helper functions for coordinate tuples and planning the part geometry with texture and decal support. I'm also considering a glow effect for parts like goggle lenses, using a flat amber color with moderate glow strength.

Now I'm picking the color palette for a dwarf character: ruddy skin tones, copper-red beard with warm highlights, and an Alliance-style blue shirt with gold trim over brown pants and leather accents, plus steel and gilt metal paints from the clockwork kit.

I'm building the skeleton hierarchy — spine chain with catmull-rom knots from hips through chest, a neck chain connecting to a head joint, then a jaw joint anchored off the head for facial articulation, with the hips joint established as the root before everything else attaches.

Now I'm sweeping the neck with a tapered radius for the skin mesh, lofting the torso stations into the shirt mesh bound to the hip/spine bones, and generating leg chains from limb-derived points parented to the hips, mirrored by side using the x-offset sign to distinguish left and right. I'm sweeping the legs with a tapered pants radius and about to add knee pad geometry.

Left hand mirrors the fist shape too. For pauldron rivets, looping through angles to place small gold spheres seems overly complex, so I'll simplify by using a cone shape instead.

Actually, a gilt rim torus laid flat would work better for the pauldron's decorative edge, rotated to lie horizontal rather than tilted -- I'll skip the tilt entirely since the dome itself doesn't need to angle, keeping the rotation simple.

Adding the hemisphere dome, spike cone, and boot/stump torus bands with iron trim details, plus wood grain texture on the stump and a metal panel finish for the anvil, which sits mounted atop the stump. Now setting up the spark particle loop...

For the eyes, I'm drafting an SVG with an almond-shaped white base, a blue iris circle, dark pupil, highlight dot, and outline, with separate mirrored brow shapes computed to curve along the head's spherical surface using position math to find where the brow rod endpoints land on the head geometry.

Working through eye position giving z around .236, then placing the nose sphere near z .25-.26 based on head surface curvature at that height. Now moving on to figuring out cheek placement.

Adding darker skin patches for blush on the cheeks, then mustache and chin details, ears as scaled spheres near the jaw, and the head sphere itself built from a surface decal. I'm also setting up braids as catmull-rom paths swept with varying radius and bone-attached, with gold beads threaded along them and a woven color pattern for the braid texture.

Now I'm adding striping along the braid axis for a woven look, gold tie caps with tassels at the ends, and positioning the beard and braids so they sit correctly against the chest and apron without clipping. I'm also sketching out the mohawk as an extruded shape with a gradient color matching the beard, plus a few finishing touches like sparks and glow effects on parts before moving to the hammer direction.

Working out the hammer head geometry next, computing handle and head positions as vectors so the head box aligns naturally along the handle's tilt, with rune-carved faces positioned on the sides of the head.

Computing the normalized perpendicular vector for the strike face offset and finalizing positions—feels ready to assemble the full code now.
